Botanical gardens by founding year.Orto Botanico di Padova: Founded in the Republic of Venice, this is generally regarded as the oldest surviving academic botanical garden, still in its original location.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Oxford Botanic Garden: England's oldest botanic garden began as a physic garden to grow medicinal plants for students of the university.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Chelsea Physic Garden: Founded by apothecaries beside the Thames, this walled garden is known for its rare medicinal plants and a setting that remains hidden in London.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Kew Gardens: This Royal Botanic Garden grew into a world-leading plant research centre and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Royal Botanic Garden Sydney: Australia's oldest botanic garden sits on Sydney Harbour's edge, and it began as the colony's first farm.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Singapore Botanic Gardens: This tropical garden in Singapore is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is famed for its orchid collection.
Botanical gardens by founding year.New York Botanical Garden: One of the largest in the United States, this garden in the Bronx has a massive glass conservatory and sits on a historic forest.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Kirstenbosch, Cape Town: Set at the foot of Table Mountain, this garden focuses on the remarkable flora of southern Africa.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Eden Project, Cornwall: Built in a former clay pit, this garden's huge biomes house the world's largest rainforest in captivity.
Botanical gardens by founding year.Gardens by the Bay: This Singapore garden is known for its giant artificial Supertrees, which collect solar energy and rainwater.

How fast these can go.Segway: Invented by Dean Kamen and unveiled in 2001, it stays upright using gyroscopes and tilt sensors that adjust many times a second.
How fast these can go.RMS Titanic: She was making roughly 22 knots on 14 April 1912 when she hit the iceberg, despite repeated ice warnings from other ships.
How fast these can go.Ford Model T: Henry Ford's moving assembly line made it so cheap that over 15 million were sold by 1927, putting ordinary families on the road.
How fast these can go.Hindenburg airship: The 245 m German zeppelin crossed the Atlantic in about two and a half days before burning at Lakehurst in 1937, killing 36.
How fast these can go.Shinkansen E5: Japan's bullet train, with a long nose that softens the boom when it enters tunnels. It has had no passenger deaths from crashes since 1964.
How fast these can go.Bugatti Veyron: Its 8-litre, 16-cylinder engine made about 1,000 horsepower, and the later Super Sport version pushed the top speed to 431 km/h.
How fast these can go.Shanghai Maglev: Opened in 2004, it floats on magnetic fields rather than wheels and covers the roughly 30 km to Pudong Airport in about eight minutes.
How fast these can go.Boeing 747 (cruising): The Queen of the Skies debuted in 1970. Its upper-deck hump exists so the nose could swing open for cargo on the freighter version.
How fast these can go.Concorde: It flew London to New York in under three and a half hours, and the heat of supersonic flight stretched its airframe by several inches.
How fast these can go.Space Shuttle in orbit: Orbiting at roughly 7.7 km per second, it circled Earth about every 90 minutes, so astronauts saw around 16 sunrises a day.

Milestones in the science of sleep.Narcolepsy named: French physician Jean-Baptiste Gelineau coined the name for sudden, uncontrollable sleep attacks.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Kleitman's sleep lab: Nathaniel Kleitman founded what is generally considered the first sleep lab, at the University of Chicago.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Sleep stages seen on EEG: Alfred Loomis's team identified distinct sleep stages with brain-wave recordings, in his private lab.
Milestones in the science of sleep.REM sleep discovered: Eugene Aserinsky and Kleitman noticed eyes darting beneath lids; this is when dreams are most vivid.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Siffre lives in a cave: Michel Siffre lived underground for two months without clocks, and his body rhythm drifted beyond 24 hours.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Randy Gardner stays awake: The teenager stayed awake 11 days (264 hours) for a science fair and recovered after sleeping.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Stanford sleep clinic opens: William Dement's clinic was the first to treat sleep disorders systematically.
Milestones in the science of sleep.CPAP for sleep apnea: Colin Sullivan in Australia developed it; a mask delivers air pressure that keeps the airway open.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Ambien approved: Zolpidem, the best-known 'Z-drug', reached the US market in 1992.
Milestones in the science of sleep.Nobel for body clock genes: Hall, Rosbash and Young won for finding the genes behind circadian rhythm in fruit flies.

From planting to first harvest.Microgreens: Tiny seedlings of vegetables or herbs, they became popular in San Francisco restaurants in the 1980s.
From planting to first harvest.Radish: Herodotus wrote that radishes, onions and garlic fed the workers who built the pyramids.
From planting to first harvest.Lettuce: Romaine takes its name from the French word for Roman, and ancient Romans prized lettuce.
From planting to first harvest.Carrot: Carrots contain beta-carotene, but eating them does not give night vision; Britain spread that myth in WWII to hide its radar.
From planting to first harvest.Potato: It first reached Europe from the Andes in the 1500s and was long viewed with suspicion.
From planting to first harvest.Garlic: Planted in autumn, it forms a bulb with cloves; cloves were found in Tutankhamun's tomb.
From planting to first harvest.Pineapple: A pineapple is really a cluster of fruits fused together, and its name comes from its pine-cone look.
From planting to first harvest.Asparagus: A long-lived plant, it is cut when the spears are young and can produce for many years.
From planting to first harvest.Apple tree from seed: Seedling apples seldom resemble their parent, so orchard trees are grafted clones.
From planting to first harvest.Oak (first acorns): An oak may not produce acorns until about 40, and a mature one can drop thousands in a year.

English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Edward III: Claiming the French throne, he launched the Hundred Years' War and founded the Order of the Garter during a 50-year reign.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Richard II: He became king at ten, and at fourteen personally faced the rebels of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt, promising reforms he later reversed.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Henry IV: Seized the crown from his cousin Richard II in 1399, founding the Lancastrian line, then spent much of his reign fighting rebellions.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Henry V: Won a stunning victory at Agincourt in 1415 against a larger French army, but died of illness at 35, leaving a baby son.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Henry VI: King at nine months old, his bouts of mental illness helped push England into the Wars of the Roses; he also founded Eton College.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Edward IV: The first Yorkist king, he was around 6 foot 4, and briefly lost the throne in 1470 before winning it back the next year.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Richard III: The last Plantagenet king died at Bosworth Field; his skeleton, curved spine and all, was found under a Leicester car park in 2012.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Henry VII: After winning at Bosworth he founded the Tudor dynasty, and was so thrifty that he left the crown a full treasury.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Henry VIII: He broke with Rome to marry Anne Boleyn, created the Church of England, and went on to marry six times.
English kings from Edward III to the Tud.Edward VI: Crowned at nine and dead at fifteen, he pushed England firmly toward Protestantism, then named Lady Jane Grey as his heir.

Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Nitrous oxide for teeth: Dentist Horace Wells tried laughing gas himself to pull a tooth in 1844, but his public demonstration the next year flopped.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Ether: William Morton's 1846 demonstration at Massachusetts General showed painless surgery, and the room is now called the Ether Dome.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Cocaine eye anesthesia: A young Viennese eye doctor, Carl Koller, showed it numbed the cornea, launching modern local anaesthesia.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Aspirin: Bayer began selling it in 1899, from a synthetic version of a compound found in willow bark.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Novocaine: Chemist Alfred Einhorn created procaine as a safer substitute for cocaine, and the trade name stuck with dental shots.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Thiopental: Sold as Sodium Pentothal, it was also dubbed truth serum, though it does not make anyone honest.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Lidocaine: Also called lignocaine, it was developed in Sweden and is still a standard numbing agent and a heart-rhythm treatment.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Fentanyl: Paul Janssen developed it, and it is roughly 50 to 100 times stronger than morphine, so tiny dosing errors can be deadly.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Ibuprofen: Developed by researchers at Boots in Britain, it was first sold as Brufen and fights both pain and inflammation.
Anesthetics and painkillers, by debut.Propofol: A milky white injection, it is the go-to sedative for operations and became infamous after Michael Jackson's death.

When these companies took their new name.Brad's Drink → Pepsi-Cola: The pharmacist Caleb Bradham invented this cola in New Bern, North Carolina, and renamed it for 'dyspepsia', as he marketed it as a digestive aid.
When these companies took their new name.Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo → Sony: The name Sony blends the Latin 'sonus' (sound) with the American slang 'sonny', chosen so it would be easy to say in any language.
When these companies took their new name.Blue Ribbon Sports → Nike: The name comes from Nike, the Greek goddess of victory. The firm began by importing Japanese running shoes, and its swoosh logo cost just $35.
When these companies took their new name.Kentucky Fried Chicken → KFC: The chain shortened its name partly to downplay 'fried' as customers turned toward healthier eating; it also began offering other menu items.
When these companies took their new name.Andersen Consulting→Accenture: It was coined in a staff naming contest: 'Accent on the future', with the 'Acc' and 'enture' spelling out the idea of going forward.
When these companies took their new name.Philip Morris Cos. → Altria: The tobacco giant swapped to a name meant to sound like 'alter', with Latin roots meaning 'other', distancing itself from the cigarette brand.
When these companies took their new name.Weight Watchers → WW: The diet company rebranded to stress wellness rather than weighing, after decades since its founding by a Queens housewife in 1963.
When these companies took their new name.Dunkin' Donuts → Dunkin': The coffee and doughnut chain dropped 'Donuts' to stress its drinks, which already made up most of its sales, after about 70 years.
When these companies took their new name.Facebook Inc. → Meta: The social network renamed its parent company for 'metaverse' ambitions; the new name echoes the Greek 'meta', meaning beyond.
When these companies took their new name.Twitter → X: Elon Musk renamed the site, with 'X' having been a long-held brand idea of his, and the blue bird logo retired after over 15 years.

Distance from New York City.Philadelphia: William Penn founded this city in 1682, and its name is Greek for 'brotherly love'. It was the US capital for most of the 1790s.
Distance from New York City.Boston: The Massachusetts capital was founded by Puritans in 1630, and its Freedom Trail passes sites of the American Revolution.
Distance from New York City.Toronto: Canada's biggest city sits on the shore of Lake Ontario, and its CN Tower was the world's tallest freestanding structure for decades.
Distance from New York City.Chicago: A city that grew where the Chicago River meets Lake Michigan, it reversed the river's flow in 1900 to keep sewage out of its drinking water.
Distance from New York City.Miami: Florida's biggest city by metro area grew from a railroad extension, and rising seas make it one of the cities most threatened by flooding.
Distance from New York City.Los Angeles: The Hollywood sign originally read 'Hollywoodland' in 1923, and it was built as a real estate ad meant to last only about a year and a half.
Distance from New York City.London: London lies about 5,570 km away, and the Concorde crossed that distance in under three and a half hours on a good day.
Distance from New York City.Rio de Janeiro: Brazil's second-largest city sits under Christ the Redeemer, a statue 30 m tall that is perched on Corcovado mountain.
Distance from New York City.Tokyo: Tokyo is one of the world's biggest metropolitan areas, with over 35 million people in its greater region, and it was called Edo until 1868.
Distance from New York City.Sydney: Sydney Opera House's sail-like roof shells are covered with over a million glossy white and cream tiles made in Sweden.

Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.The Piper at the Gates of Dawn: Mostly written by Syd Barrett, this psychedelic debut takes its title from a chapter of Kenneth Grahame's children's classic The Wind in the Willows.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.Meddle: The 23-minute 'Echoes' took up a whole side, and the opener 'One of These Days' has two basses run through an echo unit, plus a growled line.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.The Dark Side of the Moon: It spent over 700 weeks on the Billboard 200, and its prism-and-rainbow cover has become one of the best-known album designs ever.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.Wish You Were Here: The opener 'Shine On You Crazy Diamond' honors Syd Barrett, who legendarily turned up unrecognizable during the sessions, his head shaved.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.Animals: The cover shows a pig floating over Battersea Power Station. The inflatable broke free during the shoot and drifted into Heathrow's flight path.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.The Wall: Its 'Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2' was a UK Christmas number one in 1979, and the show featured a wall built on stage.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.The Final Cut: Roger Waters wrote it all, and it was the last album with him, and it is dedicated to his father, who was killed in World War II.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.A Momentary Lapse of Reason: This was the first album after Waters left, and the two sides then sued each other over the right to use the band name.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.The Division Bell: Author Douglas Adams helped name this album, and its closing track 'High Hopes' ends with a church bell, while the cover has giant metal heads.
Pink Floyd studio albums, in order.The Endless River: Built from unused 1993 recordings, this mostly instrumental album was a tribute to keyboardist Richard Wright, who died in 2008.

When these strange taxes began.Urine tax (Rome): Emperor Vespasian taxed the urine collected from public toilets, used by tanners and launderers, and told his son money does not stink.
When these strange taxes began.Window tax (England): Some owners bricked up windows to pay less, and those blank fills are still visible on old British houses.
When these strange taxes began.Beard tax (Russia): Peter the Great imposed it to push his nobles toward Western fashion, and payers carried a token proving they had paid.
When these strange taxes began.Candle tax (Britain): Beeswax candles were a rich person's light; poorer homes used smoky candles made of animal fat, called tallow.
When these strange taxes began.Wallpaper tax (Britain): Wallpaper became fashionable in 18th-century England as a cheaper stand-in for tapestries and painted panels.
When these strange taxes began.Glass tax (Britain): It lasted a century and was repealed in 1845; its weight-based charge made makers favor thin glass.
When these strange taxes began.Hat tax (Britain): Each hat had to carry a stamp showing the duty had been paid.
When these strange taxes began.Hair powder tax (Britain): Wearers of powder were nicknamed guinea pigs after the guinea paid, and the tax helped end powdered hair as a fashion.
When these strange taxes began.Dog tax (Britain): Britain's dog licence lasted until 1987, when it cost 37p.
When these strange taxes began.Fat tax (Denmark): It taxed saturated fat in foods, and was scrapped after just about a year, in 2012.

Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Reuben: Reuben lost his firstborn rights after sleeping with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Jacob later passed him over in his final blessing.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Levi: His descendants became the priests of Israel, and the tribe was given no land of its own but towns scattered among the others.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Judah: His tribe produced King David, and the words Jew and Judea both come from his name.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Dan: Samson, the strongman of the Book of Judges, came from this tribe, and his name means he judged, according to the story of his birth.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Naphtali: Jacob's blessing compares him to a doe let loose; he was the second son of Rachel's maid Bilhah, and full brother to Dan.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Gad: His name is often explained as meaning fortune or luck, and his mother was Leah's maid Zilpah, who also bore Asher.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Issachar: He was born after Leah traded mandrakes, a plant thought to aid fertility, with Rachel in exchange for a night with Jacob.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Zebulun: Jacob predicted this son would live by the seashore and become a haven for ships, and the tribe was later linked to the coast.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Joseph: His brothers sold him into slavery, but he rose to become ruler under Pharaoh in Egypt, and his coat of many colors is famous.
Sons of Jacob, by birth order.Benjamin: His mother Rachel died giving birth to him, naming him Ben-oni, son of my sorrow, a name Jacob changed to son of the right hand.

US national parks by area.Acadia: It is in Maine, the first national park east of the Mississippi, and Cadillac Mountain is among the first places in the US to see the sunrise.
US national parks by area.Zion: Hikers wade the Virgin River on the Narrows hike through its slot canyon.
US national parks by area.Yosemite: El Capitan, a giant granite wall, draws climbers from around the world.
US national parks by area.Grand Canyon: It is about 446 km long and up to about 1.8 km deep.
US national parks by area.Everglades: It is the only place on Earth where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.
US national parks by area.Yellowstone: It was America's first national park, established in 1872, and holds most of the world's geysers.
US national parks by area.Death Valley: The hottest air temperature ever recorded, 56.7 °C, was measured here in 1913.
US national parks by area.Denali: It is home to North America's tallest peak, Denali, at about 6,190 m.
US national parks by area.Gates of the Arctic: It has no roads or trails and is one of the least visited parks.
US national parks by area.Wrangell–St. Elias: It is the largest park, nearly four times the size of Yellowstone, and part of a huge UNESCO World Heritage site.

Distances between famous city pairs.Tel Aviv to Jerusalem: An hour or so by road, it follows the line of an 1892 railway between Jaffa and Jerusalem, among the oldest in the region.
Distances between famous city pairs.London to Paris: Eurostar covers it in about two hours and twenty minutes, since the Channel Tunnel opened in 1994.
Distances between famous city pairs.Berlin to Munich: Fast ICE trains take about four hours, since a new high-speed line was opened in 2017 cutting the time.
Distances between famous city pairs.Moscow to St Petersburg: Legend says Tsar Nicholas I drew the railway line between them with a ruler, leaving a bump where his finger slipped.
Distances between famous city pairs.New York to Chicago: The two cities are about two hours apart by air, but the famous 20th Century Limited train covered it overnight.
Distances between famous city pairs.Madrid to Moscow: A flight takes around five hours, from the Iberian Peninsula across the width of Europe to Russia.
Distances between famous city pairs.London to New York: Concorde flew it in under three and a half hours, with a record of about 2 hours 52 minutes.
Distances between famous city pairs.Cairo to Cape Town: Cecil Rhodes dreamed of a railway from Cape to Cairo, but it was never finished, and the route still has gaps.
Distances between famous city pairs.Los Angeles to Sydney: The flight crosses the International Date Line, so you lose a calendar day on the way, and it takes about 15 hours.
Distances between famous city pairs.London to Auckland: Britain's antipode, the point directly opposite on Earth, lies near New Zealand, so the two are almost as far apart as possible.

When these market indexes and funds bega.Dow Jones Industrial Average: Charles Dow launched it with just 12 industrial companies, a tiny group compared with today's 30.
When these market indexes and funds bega.Nikkei 225: Compiled by the newspaper Nihon Keizai Shimbun, it peaked in 1989 and did not regain that high until 2024.
When these market indexes and funds bega.S&P 500: It tracks 500 of the largest US companies and covers about 80 percent of the market's total value.
When these market indexes and funds bega.Hang Seng Index: It tracks the largest Hong Kong stocks and takes its name from Hang Seng Bank.
When these market indexes and funds bega.Nasdaq Composite: Heavily weighted toward technology, it hit a dot-com peak in March 2000.
When these market indexes and funds bega.FTSE 100: Londoners nickname it the 'Footsie', and it tracks the 100 largest companies on the London Stock Exchange.
When these market indexes and funds bega.DAX: Frankfurt's blue-chip index now tracks 40 companies.
When these market indexes and funds bega.SPDR S&P 500 ETF: Nicknamed 'Spider', it was the first US exchange-traded fund and remains among the largest.
When these market indexes and funds bega.Euro Stoxx 50: It follows 50 blue-chip eurozone companies, launched a year before the euro itself.
When these market indexes and funds bega.S&P/ASX 200: It is Australia's benchmark index, covering the 200 largest companies on the Australian exchange.

Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Bulbasaur: The first Pokémon in the Pokédex, it carries a plant bulb on its back that grows as it matures.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Pikachu: The electric mouse mascot stores electricity in its cheeks, and it became the face of the franchise.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Jigglypuff: Its song puts everyone who hears it to sleep, to the annoyance of its fans.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Psyduck: It is constantly beset by headaches, and its odd psychic powers awaken when the headache worsens.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Gengar: This ghost Pokémon is said to be a shadow that lurks in dark corners, evolved from Haunter by trade.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Magikarp: The weak fish evolves into the powerful Gyarados at level 20.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Eevee: It can evolve into eight different forms, nicknamed the 'Eeveelutions'.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Snorlax: It sleeps most of the day and famously blocks roads in the Kanto games.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Mewtwo: It is a genetically engineered clone of Mew.
Pokédex numbers of these Pokémon.Lucario: The Aura Pokémon, introduced in the fourth generation, senses auras to find opponents.

European countries by population.Liechtenstein: Known for dental products maker Ivoclar and low taxes, this tiny principality is one of only two doubly landlocked countries.
European countries by population.Iceland: With no standing army, it also has the world's oldest parliament, the Althing, founded around 930.
European countries by population.Luxembourg: The only remaining sovereign grand duchy, it has one of the highest GDPs per person in Europe.
European countries by population.Ireland: Before the Famine of the 1840s the island held about 8 million people; emigration shrank it for a century.
European countries by population.Sweden: Its people live mostly in the south, and the country has stayed out of wars for over two centuries.
European countries by population.Netherlands: A quarter of the country lies below sea level, and it is among the most densely populated countries in the world.
European countries by population.Poland: Warsaw's Old Town was rebuilt after World War II, partly using 18th-century paintings as a guide.
European countries by population.Spain: Madrid's Sobrino de Botín, from 1725, is recognized by Guinness as the world's oldest restaurant.
European countries by population.Italy: Home to more UNESCO World Heritage sites than almost any other country.
European countries by population.Germany: The most populous EU country was reunified in 1990, a year after the Berlin Wall fell.

Powers and factorials by value.5!: Five factorial counts the ways to arrange five books on a shelf, 120 of them.
Powers and factorials by value.3^5: That is also the number of outcomes from five rounds of a three-way choice, like rock-paper-scissors.
Powers and factorials by value.4^4: It's also 2 to the 8th power, the number of values a single byte can hold.
Powers and factorials by value.7^3: 343 is also roughly the speed of sound in air in meters per second at about 20 degrees C.
Powers and factorials by value.6!: It's also the number of degrees in two full turns, a coincidence handy for remembering it.
Powers and factorials by value.10^3: The metric prefix kilo means 10 cubed, which is why a kilogram is a thousand grams.
Powers and factorials by value.2^10: The near-thousand of computing; a kibibyte is 1,024 bytes, the reason 'kilo' wasn't exactly 1,000 in old computer talk.
Powers and factorials by value.3^7: On a Rubik's cube, the eight corner pieces can be twisted in 3 to the 7th ways, as the eighth is forced by the others.
Powers and factorials by value.8!: Eight people can queue in this many orders, while a deck of 52 cards can be shuffled in about 8 followed by 67 zeros.
Powers and factorials by value.2^16: It's the number of values a 16-bit integer can hold, and of network ports numbered 0 to 65,535.

Distance from Sydney.Canberra: Australia's capital was a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne, purpose-built in the early 1900s. Its lake is named after its American designer, Walter Burley Griffin.
Distance from Sydney.Melbourne: Australia's second-largest city and a long-time rival of Sydney. It was the national capital until 1927 and is famed for its coffee and laneways.
Distance from Sydney.Hobart: Tasmania's capital is Australia's second-oldest city, founded in 1804. Its Salamanca Market and the nearby MONA museum draw crowds.
Distance from Sydney.Auckland: New Zealand's largest city sits on a volcanic field of about 50 volcanoes, and it is known as the City of Sails for its many boats.
Distance from Sydney.Perth: Perth is often called the most isolated major city on Earth. Its nearest city of similar size, Adelaide, is over 2,000 km away.
Distance from Sydney.Singapore: This island city-state is one of the world's busiest ports and has no natural lakes; much of its drinking water is recycled or imported.
Distance from Sydney.Tokyo: Japan's capital is the most populous metropolitan area on Earth, with over 35 million people in the greater region.
Distance from Sydney.Santiago, Chile: Chile's capital sits in a valley ringed by the Andes, and on clear days snowy peaks are visible from the city streets.
Distance from Sydney.Los Angeles: The City of Angels sits across the Pacific from Sydney. Flights between them take about 13 hours and cross the date line, arriving earlier than you departed.
Distance from Sydney.London: Almost the opposite side of the globe for Sydney. The two cities are about as far apart as major cities get, with a 9 to 11 hour clock gap.

Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.Uruguay: The hosts won the first World Cup in 1930 in Montevideo, beating Argentina 4-2 in the final. Uruguay has two official titles but four stars, counting Olympic golds.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.Italy: Hosts and under Mussolini's Fascist regime, Italy won the 1934 tournament, and again in 1938, the first nation to win back-to-back World Cups.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.West Germany: The "Miracle of Bern": West Germany beat the great Hungary team 3-2 in the final, after losing 8-3 to them in the group stage.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.Brazil: Brazil won in Sweden, led by a 17-year-old Pele, who scored twice in the final. Brazil went on to win five titles in total, the most of any nation.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.England: The only men's title for England came at Wembley, with Geoff Hurst's hat-trick in the final against West Germany, and a ball that may or may not have crossed the line.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.Argentina: Argentina won as hosts, with Mario Kempes scoring twice in the final against the Netherlands, in a tournament played during military rule.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.USA (women): The USA women won the first Women's World Cup in China in 1991, a tournament little noticed at the time, and have four titles in total.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.France: France won as hosts, beating Brazil 3-0, with two Zinedine Zidane headers, and won again in 2018.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.Spain: La Roja won in South Africa after a 1-0 win over the Netherlands, with Iniesta's goal in extra time, and had won Euro 2008 and 2012.
Nations' first World Cup title (men or w.Japan (women): Japan's Nadeshiko beat the USA on penalties in the 2011 final in Germany, becoming the first Asian team to win a senior World Cup.

First flights of famous helicopters.Sikorsky VS-300: Igor Sikorsky's 1939 prototype was tethered at first. It made the single-rotor design, a main rotor and a tail rotor, the standard for helicopters.
First flights of famous helicopters.Sikorsky R-4: The first mass-produced helicopter in the world, it was used in 1944 to rescue downed airmen in Burma, the first helicopter combat rescue.
First flights of famous helicopters.Bell 47: A bubble-canopy helicopter that was a Korean War medevac icon, seen in the TV series M*A*S*H, and was the first helicopter certified for civilian use.
First flights of famous helicopters.Bell UH-1 Huey: The "Huey" became the symbol of the Vietnam War, with its distinctive "whop-whop" sound made by its rotor blades, and flew thousands of missions.
First flights of famous helicopters.Boeing CH-47 Chinook: This tandem-rotor heavy-lifter has been in service for decades, and is still used for moving large loads. It first flew in 1961.
First flights of famous helicopters.Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk: This is the US Army's main utility helicopter, named for a Sauk leader, and used in the Mogadishu raid of 1993. A Black Hawk can carry 11 troops.
First flights of famous helicopters.AH-64 Apache: The US Army's main attack helicopter is famous for its Hellfire missiles and 30 mm chain gun. It first flew in 1975 and has seen combat in Iraq and Afghanistan.
First flights of famous helicopters.V-22 Osprey: A tiltrotor aircraft, which takes off like a helicopter and flies like a plane by swiveling its rotors forward. Its development was long and troubled.
First flights of famous helicopters.Eurocopter Tiger: A European attack helicopter by a Franco-German firm, in service since the 2000s with France, Germany, Spain and Australia.
First flights of famous helicopters.Ingenuity, on Mars: The small NASA helicopter made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet on April 19, 2021, in an atmosphere only about 1 percent as dense as Earth's.

Desert animals by weight.Deathstalker scorpion: Like all scorpions it glows blue-green under ultraviolet light, which makes night hunting for them easy.
Desert animals by weight.Lesser Egyptian jerboa: This tiny hopper leaps like a miniature kangaroo, and gets almost all its water from the seeds it eats.
Desert animals by weight.Greater roadrunner: It can sprint at roughly 30 km/h, and it is quick enough to catch and kill rattlesnakes.
Desert animals by weight.Meerkat: Colonies take turns as lookouts, standing on hind legs to scan for hawks while others dig for insects in the Kalahari.
Desert animals by weight.Fennec fox: Its huge ears give off body heat to keep it cool and also pick up the sound of insects moving underground.
Desert animals by weight.Desert tortoise: It spends most of its life underground in burrows, and can store a lot of water in its bladder.
Desert animals by weight.Striped hyena: It scavenges at night across North Africa and Asia, and raises its mane to look bigger when threatened.
Desert animals by weight.Arabian oryx: It was extinct in the wild by 1972, and was brought back from captive herds. It may have inspired the unicorn legend.
Desert animals by weight.Ostrich: The largest living bird has eyes larger than its brain, and can sprint around 70 km/h.
Desert animals by weight.Dromedary camel: The hump stores fat, not water, and a thirsty camel can drink over 100 litres in a few minutes.

When these instruments and music gadgets.Metronome (patented): Johann Maelzel patented it after borrowing the design from Dietrich Winkel, and Beethoven was one of its early enthusiasts.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Accordion (patented): Patented in Vienna by Cyrill Demian, its bellows push air over metal reeds, working much like a giant harmonica.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Saxophone (patented): Belgian Adolphe Sax patented it, and despite its brass body it counts as a woodwind because it uses a reed.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Sousaphone: A bandmaster's marching tuba named for John Philip Sousa, wrapped around the player's body so the bell rises over the head.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Theremin: Played without touching it: hand movements near two antennas control pitch and volume. Its inventor was Léon Theremin.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Hammond organ: Spinning tonewheels, not pipes, make its sound, which made it a cheaper alternative for churches in the Great Depression.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Gibson Les Paul: Named for the jazz guitarist who also pioneered multitrack recording, it was the first solid-body rival to Fender's designs.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Fender Stratocaster: Its contoured body and three pickups made it the guitar of Hendrix, Clapton and many more.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Moog synthesizer: Robert Moog's keyboard synth reached a mass audience through Wendy Carlos's 1968 album Switched-On Bach.
When these instruments and music gadgets.Roland TR-808: It was a commercial flop at first, but its boomy bass drum and handclaps became the sound of hip-hop and dance.

Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.Count Orlok: Max Schreck's Count Orlok came from an unauthorized Dracula; Bram Stoker's widow sued and had copies ordered destroyed, but some survived.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.Dracula (Bela Lugosi): Bela Lugosi had played Dracula on Broadway, and his Hungarian accent and cape shaped the image of the vampire for generations.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.The Mummy (Boris Karloff): Boris Karloff, also Frankenstein's monster, spent hours in makeup to become Imhotep, a film inspired by the craze after Tutankhamun's tomb.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.Godzilla: Gojira blends the Japanese words for gorilla and whale; the 1954 film reflected nuclear fears after Hiroshima and a fishing boat's H-bomb exposure.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.The Blob: The Blob gave Steve McQueen his first leading role, and the gooey monster was made from silicone dyed red.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.Bruce the shark from Jaws: The mechanical shark was nicknamed Bruce, after Spielberg's lawyer, and kept breaking in salt water, so it appears late, making the film scarier.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.The Xenomorph from Alien: Swiss artist H. R. Giger designed the creature, and Bolaji Badejo, a student over two meters tall, wore the suit for the film.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.Gremlins: The rules are no light, no water, no food after midnight; the word gremlin was popularized by RAF pilots blaming mishaps in World War II.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.The Predator: Kevin Peter Hall, over two meters tall, played the hunter in the suit, and the film's alien was famously a trophy-hunting extraterrestrial.
Movie monsters by their big-screen debut.The Cloverfield monster: The film was shot like found footage on a handheld camera, and its marketing kept the title and the monster a secret until release.

Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.Left Shift: Shift is named for old typewriters, where pressing it physically shifted the carriage so the machine printed capitals.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.Z: On German keyboards Z and Y swap places, giving a layout called QWERTZ, because Z is far commoner in German.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.X: X is the cut shortcut (Ctrl+X) because the letter looks like a pair of open scissors, which makes it easy to remember.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.C: Ctrl+C means copy in most programs, but in a terminal window it interrupts the running program instead.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.V: Ctrl+V pastes, and Z, X, C and V sit side by side so undo, cut, copy and paste are one-handed shortcuts.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.B: Ctrl+B makes text bold in most word processors, a shortcut that has barely changed in decades.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.N: N sits next to M, and Ctrl+N opens a new document or window in most programs, from word processors to browsers.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.M: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000, from mille, and it is the last letter on the bottom row.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.Comma key: The word comma comes from the Greek komma, a piece cut off, and a comma marks where a sentence is cut for a breath.
Bottom-row keys on a US QWERTY keyboard.Period key: The period is called a full stop in Britain, and the same dot in a web address is spoken aloud as dot.

When construction began on these landmar.Hagia Sophia (current): Built under Justinian in under six years, its dome was the world's largest cathedral vault for roughly a thousand years.
When construction began on these landmar.Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey: The abbey crowns a tidal island in Normandy, where some of Europe's biggest tides turn the causeway into open water.
When construction began on these landmar.White Tower, London: William the Conqueror raised this keep after 1066 to overawe London; it later served as a royal prison and armoury.
When construction began on these landmar.Durham Cathedral: This Norman masterpiece was among the first to use rib vaults at scale, and it shelters the shrines of St Cuthbert and Bede.
When construction began on these landmar.Notre-Dame de Paris: Construction took nearly two centuries. A 2019 fire destroyed its spire, and the rebuilt cathedral reopened in December 2024.
When construction began on these landmar.Chartres Cathedral (Gothic): Much of its stained glass dates from the early 1200s and survives intact, including the famous deep 'Chartres blue'.
When construction began on these landmar.Alhambra (Nasrid palace): The name comes from Arabic for 'the red one', probably for its walls; Granada's palace-fortress is famed for carved stucco.
When construction began on these landmar.Malbork Castle: Built by the Teutonic Knights, this Polish fortress is often called the largest brick castle in the world by area.
When construction began on these landmar.Forbidden City: Home to 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties, this Beijing palace complex has about 980 surviving buildings.
When construction began on these landmar.Moscow Kremlin's brick walls: Ivan III hired Italian architects to rebuild the Kremlin, which is why Moscow's red walls look like Renaissance fortresses.

Gases in dry air by abundance.Xenon: This heavy noble gas fills some headlights and powers ion thrusters, such as the ones on NASA's Dawn spacecraft.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Hydrogen: The universe's most common element is scarce in air because it is so light that it escapes Earth's gravity.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Krypton: Its name means 'hidden' in Greek, and from 1960 to 1983 the metre was defined by light from krypton-86.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Methane: A greenhouse gas many times stronger than CO2 per molecule, released by wetlands, cattle, rice paddies and landfills.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Helium: Helium was spotted in the Sun's light in 1868 before anyone found it on Earth; its name comes from Helios, the Greek sun god.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Neon: Its red-orange glow in glass tubes gave neon signs their name, though other colors rely on different gases or phosphors.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Carbon dioxide: Though tiny, this share traps heat and feeds plants; it has climbed from about 280 ppm before industry to over 420 ppm.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Argon: Third most common, nearly all of it came from radioactive potassium-40 decaying in rocks; it fills double-glazed windows.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Oxygen: Air had almost none until cyanobacteria began photosynthesizing, causing a buildup over two billion years ago.
Gases in dry air by abundance.Nitrogen: It dominates the air, but life can't use it directly; bacteria and lightning must 'fix' it into forms plants can absorb.

Meteor showers by peak date.Quadrantids: Named for the lost constellation Quadrans Muralis. Its parent is probably an asteroid, 2003 EH1, rather than a comet.
Meteor showers by peak date.Lyrids: Among the oldest recorded showers, spotted by Chinese astronomers in 687 BC.
Meteor showers by peak date.Eta Aquariids: Dust left by Halley's Comet. It is best seen from the tropics and Southern Hemisphere.
Meteor showers by peak date.Southern Delta Aquariids: A steady, faint shower best seen from the Southern Hemisphere and the tropics.
Meteor showers by peak date.Perseids: Debris from Comet Swift-Tuttle. It is nicknamed the Tears of St Lawrence because it peaks near his August feast day.
Meteor showers by peak date.Draconids: Produced by Comet 21P/Giacobini-Zinner. Usually weak, it erupted into storms in 1933 and 1946.
Meteor showers by peak date.Orionids: A second shower from Halley's Comet, which crosses Earth's orbit twice a year, in May and October.
Meteor showers by peak date.Leonids: A storm roughly every 33 years. The 1833 storm, with tens of thousands an hour, helped launch meteor astronomy.
Meteor showers by peak date.Geminids: Unusually, it comes from an asteroid, 3200 Phaethon, not a comet. It is often the year's strongest shower.
Meteor showers by peak date.Ursids: Debris of Comet 8P/Tuttle. A modest shower arriving near the winter solstice.

Star Trek series premieres.The Original Series: It ran only three seasons, yet the 1966 show launched a franchise, coining 'beam me up' and the first interracial TV kiss.
Star Trek series premieres.The Animated Series: Made with Saturday-morning cartoon animation, it won an Emmy and let writers show aliens a live-action budget never allowed.
Star Trek series premieres.The Next Generation: Set about 80 years after the original, it brought Captain Picard and Data to TV and ran for seven seasons from 1987.
Star Trek series premieres.Deep Space Nine: Set on a space station instead of a starship, it was the first Trek with a Black lead, Captain Sisko, and long serial arcs.
Star Trek series premieres.Voyager: Stranded 70,000 light-years from home, this crew was led by Captain Janeway, the franchise's first female lead captain.
Star Trek series premieres.Enterprise: Set before Kirk's era, it opened with a theme song by Russell Watson, unusual for a Trek show, and ran four seasons.
Star Trek series premieres.Discovery: It was the first Trek of the streaming era, premiering on CBS All Access, and jumped ahead to the 32nd century.
Star Trek series premieres.Picard: Patrick Stewart came back as Jean-Luc Picard in his eighties, retired from Starfleet and at odds with its leaders.
Star Trek series premieres.Prodigy: Aimed at younger viewers, it follows teens who find an abandoned Starfleet ship, and it began on Paramount+ and Nickelodeon.
Star Trek series premieres.Strange New Worlds: Set aboard Captain Pike's Enterprise, it grew from a Discovery character and has a classic episode-of-the-week feel.

Medieval milestones, in order.Western Roman Empire falls: When the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed, the line ended, though the Eastern Empire went on for nearly a thousand years.
Medieval milestones, in order.Muhammad's Hijra to Medina: The year 622 begins the Islamic calendar, and Medina is now Islam's second-holiest city.
Medieval milestones, in order.Viking raid on Lindisfarne: Norse raiders hit the island monastery in Northumbria, and the attack launched the Viking Age in Britain.
Medieval milestones, in order.Leif Erikson reaches America: The Norse explorer sailed from Greenland to a place he called Vinland, 500 years before Columbus.
Medieval milestones, in order.Norman Conquest of England: William of Normandy won at Hastings, and built the Domesday Book and the Tower of London.
Medieval milestones, in order.Crusaders capture Jerusalem: Christian armies took Jerusalem after a siege in the First Crusade, and then set up a Crusader kingdom that lasted about 90 years.
Medieval milestones, in order.Magna Carta sealed: King John sealed it at Runnymede, limiting royal power, and it influenced later constitutions.
Medieval milestones, in order.Black Death reaches Europe: The plague arrived by ship in Sicily, and it killed around a third of Europe's people in a few years.
Medieval milestones, in order.Fall of Constantinople: The Ottomans under Mehmed II took the Byzantine capital, ending the Roman Empire's last remnant.
Medieval milestones, in order.Columbus reaches the Americas: Sailing for Spain, he landed in the Bahamas, and he thought he had reached Asia.

When these food brands first appeared.Lea & Perrins Worcestershire: Created by two chemists in Worcester, England, it was reportedly a failed batch forgotten in barrels, and it turned tasty after fermenting.
When these food brands first appeared.Heinz ketchup: Henry Heinz sold ketchup in clear glass bottles so buyers could see its purity, and the '57 varieties' slogan was just a catchy number.
When these food brands first appeared.Coca-Cola: Pharmacist John Pemberton invented it in Atlanta, and an early recipe included coca leaf extract.
When these food brands first appeared.Jell-O: A New York carpenter, Pearle Wait, turned a gelatin recipe into a dessert, then sold the rights for 450 dollars to the man who made it famous.
When these food brands first appeared.Oreo: Nabisco's creme sandwich cookie came out four years after Hydrox, and it's now the best-selling cookie in the US.
When these food brands first appeared.Twinkies: Hostess invented this cream-filled sponge cake, and its filling was originally banana flavored, until a wartime banana shortage.
When these food brands first appeared.Spam: Hormel's canned meat was a staple for Allied troops in World War II, and its name may be short for 'spiced ham'.
When these food brands first appeared.M&M's: Mars made candy-coated chocolates so soldiers could carry them without melting, and the name stands for Mars and Murrie.
When these food brands first appeared.Nutella: Pietro Ferrero created this chocolate-hazelnut spread to stretch scarce cocoa in postwar Italy, adding hazelnuts, plentiful in Piedmont.
When these food brands first appeared.Red Bull: Based on a Thai tonic, it was created by Austrian Dietrich Mateschitz after he discovered it while traveling in Asia.

NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Bravo: It's an Italian word of praise, shouted at performers, and it stands for B in radio spelling, second in the alphabet.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Foxtrot: Named after a ballroom dance, it stands for F, so a pilot spelling out a call sign doesn't get mixed up with a similar letter.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Hotel: The word for a place to stay stands for H, and it was chosen because it sounds distinct, even over a crackling radio.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Juliett: Spelled with two Ts, unlike the English name, so French speakers don't treat the final T as silent and misread it.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Lima: The capital of Peru, it stands for L, and it was picked because it's easy to say in many languages.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.November: It's the only code word named after a month, and it stands for N, one of 26 words standardized in the 1950s.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Papa: A familiar word for father in many languages, it stands for P in the alphabet pilots and ships use worldwide.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Romeo: Shakespeare's lover stands for R, and the code word was chosen because it's clear and distinct over a radio.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Uniform: The word for a standard outfit stands for U, and its pronunciation is carefully set as 'YOU-nee-form' in the official guide.
NATO alphabet code words, in alphabet or.Yankee: A nickname for Americans, it stands for Y, near the very end of the alphabet at number 25 of 26.

Words for people by age bracket.Vicenarian: From Latin viginti, 'twenty'; the word is rare, since people just say they are in their twenties.
Words for people by age bracket.Tricenarian: It comes from Latin triceni, meaning 'thirty each', and is seldom used outside crosswords and word lists.
Words for people by age bracket.Quadragenarian: The term comes from Latin quadrageni, 'forty each', and is one of the stranger words in this family.
Words for people by age bracket.Quinquagenarian: Quinquaginta is Latin for fifty; the double 'q' makes it a great spelling-bee test.
Words for people by age bracket.Sexagenarian: Latin sexaginta means sixty; Babylonian base-60 counting also gave us 60-minute hours and 360 degrees.
Words for people by age bracket.Septuagenarian: Its root is shared with the Septuagint, the Greek Old Testament, named for the legend of seventy translators.
Words for people by age bracket.Octogenarian: Latin octoginta means eighty; 'October' also comes from Latin octo, since it was once the eighth month.
Words for people by age bracket.Nonagenarian: Latin nonaginta means ninety; 'November' comes from the Latin for nine, as it was once the ninth month.
Words for people by age bracket.Centenarian: Japan has tens of thousands of centenarians, among the highest rates in the world.
Words for people by age bracket.Supercentenarian: Verified people over 110 are very rare; Jeanne Calment of France reached 122, the longest confirmed human life.

Scrabble face value of these animals.Ant: Colonies can hold millions of ants, and some species farm fungus or herd aphids for their sweet honeydew.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Owl: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees, and soft fringed feathers let them fly almost silently.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Moose: The largest deer, a bull moose regrows and sheds its huge antlers every year, and will wade and dive for water plants.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Koala: Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day because eucalyptus leaves give little energy, and their fingerprints resemble ours.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Yak: Domesticated in the Himalaya and Tibetan Plateau, yaks thrive above 4,000 metres and provide milk, wool and transport.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Fox: Foxes hear low sounds so well that they can detect rodents burrowing under snow.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Giraffe: A giraffe has the same seven neck vertebrae as you, each one just far longer, up to about 25 cm.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Zebra: Every zebra's stripe pattern is unique, and the stripes may help deter biting flies.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Jackal: Golden jackals often hunt in pairs, and older offspring may stay to help raise the next litter.
Scrabble face value of these animals.Quokka: This small Australian marsupial, found mostly on Rottnest Island, looks like it is smiling and has little fear of people.

How often these letters appear in Englis.Z: Americans say "zee" while most of the English-speaking world says "zed", and in Scrabble this rare letter is worth 10 points.
How often these letters appear in Englis.K: The K in knife and knight was once pronounced, but the sound faded from English speech centuries ago while the spelling stayed.
How often these letters appear in Englis.B: B went silent in debt and doubt, where scholars added it to echo the Latin roots, even though the word had lost it.
How often these letters appear in Englis.G: The Romans made G by adding a bar to C, so the two letters share an ancestor and the same Phoenician source.
How often these letters appear in Englis.C: C is a famously redundant letter: it sounds like K in cat and like S in city, so it could be dropped without losing sounds.
How often these letters appear in Englis.D: Its ancestor was the Phoenician daleth, thought to depict a door, and the Greek delta is the same letter turned into a triangle.
How often these letters appear in Englis.R: On Wheel of Fortune's final round, R is one of the free letters, alongside S, T, L, N and E, because they are so common.
How often these letters appear in Englis.I: As a pronoun, I is always capitalized in English, a habit that has no match in most other European languages.
How often these letters appear in Englis.T: T is the most common consonant in English, and it starts the most frequent word, "the".
How often these letters appear in Englis.E: Georges Perec wrote a full novel, La Disparition, without using E at all, and its English translation, A Void, does the same.

Swahili numbers, by the value they name.moja: Swahili clocks start at dawn, so saa moja, hour one, means 7 a.m., and the language is spoken by over 100 million people.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.mbili: The word is a Bantu original, and Swahili is East Africa's lingua franca across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and beyond.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.tatu: To say third, Swahili adds a particle: wa tatu, as in the third person or third place.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.nne: Many Bantu languages share a similar root for four, a sign of how far the Bantu family spread across the continent.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.tano: Counting to five on one hand is universal, and Swahili's tano belongs to the Bantu stock that many African languages share.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.sita: Six was borrowed from Arabic sitta, a trace of centuries of Indian Ocean trade along the Swahili coast.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.saba: Seven is another Arabic loan, from sab'a, showing the monsoon trade links between the coast and Arabia.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.nane: Tanzania marks Nane Nane, "eight eight", on August 8 as a farmers' holiday.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.tisa: Nine is borrowed from Arabic tis'a, so the numbers sita, saba and tisa all reveal coastal Arabic influence.
Swahili numbers, by the value they name.kumi: Kumi is the base for larger numbers: eleven is kumi na moja, literally ten and one.

When these record labels were founded.Columbia: Columbia is the oldest surviving record label, and began by selling phonograph cylinders and equipment.
When these record labels were founded.Decca: Decca started in Britain and famously turned down The Beatles in 1962, saying guitar groups were on their way out.
When these record labels were founded.Blue Note: Blue Note was founded by German émigrés and became the label of hard bop, with legends like Art Blakey and Thelonious Monk.
When these record labels were founded.Atlantic: Atlantic was founded by Ahmet Ertegun and Herb Abramson, and signed Ray Charles, Aretha Franklin and Led Zeppelin.
When these record labels were founded.Sun Records: Sam Phillips's studio in Memphis launched Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash and Jerry Lee Lewis.
When these record labels were founded.Motown: Berry Gordy started Motown in Detroit with an 800 dollar loan, and created the sound of the Supremes and Stevie Wonder.
When these record labels were founded.Apple Records: The Beatles formed this label, and its green apple logo was a pun on the Apple Computer name that later led to a lawsuit.
When these record labels were founded.Def Jam: Rick Rubin and Russell Simmons started it in a New York dorm room, and it helped make hip-hop mainstream with Run-DMC and LL Cool J.
When these record labels were founded.Sub Pop: The Seattle label helped define grunge, signing Nirvana before they were famous, and sold Nirvana's debut Bleach for 606 dollars.
When these record labels were founded.Death Row: Founded by Dr. Dre and Suge Knight, the label was home to Tupac Shakur and Snoop Dogg and defined West Coast hip-hop.

Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Titanic sinks: A first-class letter cost 2 cents in 1912, so a message about the ship's loss could cross the country for pocket change.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Pearl Harbor attack: The 3-cent rate held steady for years, and the attack that brought the US into World War II came with the stamp price unchanged.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Moon landing: The stamp cost 6 cents, and soon afterwards a 10-cent airmail stamp was issued to celebrate the first Moon landing.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Nixon resigns: By 1974 first-class postage had reached 10 cents, a big jump from the 3-cent letter of the 1940s.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Elvis dies: The 13-cent rate was in force in 1977, and in 1993 the public voted to pick a young Elvis for a commemorative stamp.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Live Aid concert: The 1985 benefit concert for Ethiopian famine relief took place when a first-class stamp cost 22 cents in the United States.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Berlin Wall falls: A 25-cent stamp covered a letter when the Wall opened on 9 November 1989, ending 28 years of division in Berlin.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.9/11 attacks: The stamp cost 34 cents in 2001, then rose to 37 cents the next year, as postal prices crept up gradually.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.Obama's first inauguration: It was 42 cents when the first Black US president took office, before a rise to 44 cents later that year.
Cost of a US stamp when this happened.COVID declared a pandemic: Since 2007 'Forever' stamps stay valid whatever the price later rises to, so one bought then still covers a letter now.

Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Tull's seed drill: Jethro Tull's horse-drawn machine planted seeds in neat rows, replacing scattering by hand, and it's often seen as a start of modern farming.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Meikle's threshing machine: The Scottish engineer's machine separated grain from stalks, replacing the flail and the long hours of winter hand labour.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.McCormick's reaper: Cyrus McCormick's horse-drawn machine cut grain much faster than hand scythes and helped open up the American prairies.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Deere's steel plow: Blacksmith John Deere is said to have made his first self-scouring plow from a broken sawblade, to cut sticky prairie soil.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Refrigerated ship cargo: The SS Dunedin carried frozen New Zealand meat to Britain, proving that distant farms could feed faraway cities.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Gasoline tractor: John Froelich built it in Iowa, and engines soon began to replace the horses and mules that had pulled farm machinery.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Synthetic fertilizer plant: The Haber-Bosch process pulled nitrogen from the air to make fertiliser, and today it helps feed roughly half the world.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.DDT used as insecticide: Paul Müller discovered its insecticidal power, winning a Nobel Prize, before Rachel Carson's Silent Spring exposed its harm.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Flavr Savr GM tomato: It was the first genetically engineered food approved for sale, bred to ripen without going soft, but it didn't last long on shelves.
Farming inventions and breakthroughs.Golden rice: Engineered with beta-carotene to fight vitamin A deficiency, this rice has a golden-orange color, and remains controversial.

Memorable World Cup moments.The Maracanazo: Brazil lost 2-1 to Uruguay in front of nearly 200,000 people at the Maracana, in what Brazilians still call a national tragedy.
Memorable World Cup moments.Teenage Pele wins the Cup: At just 17, he scored twice in the 5-2 final against Sweden, and wept on the pitch in joy.
Memorable World Cup moments.Hurst's hat-trick in the final: Geoff Hurst's three goals were the first men's final hat-trick, matched only by Kylian Mbappé in 2022.
Memorable World Cup moments.Banks's save from Pele: Gordon Banks's diving save from Pelé's header is regularly called the greatest save ever made.
Memorable World Cup moments.Maradona's Hand of God: Against England, he punched the ball in, then minutes later scored the 'Goal of the Century' after dribbling past five players.
Memorable World Cup moments.Baggio's penalty miss: His penalty sailed over the bar in the Pasadena shootout, handing Brazil the title.
Memorable World Cup moments.Zidane's headbutt: In his last match, Zidane butted Marco Materazzi in extra time, and Italy won on penalties.
Memorable World Cup moments.Iniesta's winner: The goal in extra time against the Netherlands gave Spain its first title, and he had a tribute to a late friend under his shirt.
Memorable World Cup moments.Gotze's winner: A young substitute volleyed in extra time at the Maracana to give Germany a fourth title.
Memorable World Cup moments.Messi lifts the trophy: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw, with Kylian Mbappé scoring a hat-trick in defeat.

When these debut albums came out.Elvis Presley: His debut was the first rock and roll album to reach number one on the US album chart. The cover inspired The Clash's London Calling.
When these debut albums came out.Are You Experienced: Hendrix's debut included Purple Haze, and the UK and US versions had different track lists. It showed the power of electric guitar.
When these debut albums came out.Led Zeppelin (debut): Reportedly recorded in about 36 hours of studio time, this album introduced Jimmy Page's riffs. It opened with Good Times Bad Times.
When these debut albums came out.Horses (Patti Smith): John Cale produced this poet-singer's debut, and Robert Mapplethorpe photographed the stark cover. It's often seen as a starting point for punk.
When these debut albums came out.Never Mind the Bollocks: The Sex Pistols' only studio album caused trouble because of the title, and a shop owner was prosecuted for displaying it. He was acquitted.
When these debut albums came out.Appetite for Destruction: It is often said to be the best-selling debut album in US history. Axl Rose and Slash's band came out of Los Angeles.
When these debut albums came out.Ten (Pearl Jam): Pearl Jam named it after basketball star Mookie Blaylock's jersey number. Alive, Even Flow and Jeremy come from this record.
When these debut albums came out.Definitely Maybe: Oasis's debut was the fastest-selling debut in UK history at the time. It includes Live Forever and Supersonic.
When these debut albums came out.Is This It (The Strokes): The Strokes' garage-rock debut brought guitar bands back. The US version replaced one track after a post-9/11 sensitivity about its lyrics.
When these debut albums came out.Pure Heroine (Lorde): Lorde wrote it while still a teenager from New Zealand. Its hit single Royals topped the US chart and mocked pop-star excess.

Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Princess Aurora is born: Disney's 1959 Sleeping Beauty cost about 6 million dollars and flopped at first, but it is now loved and has a score adapted from Tchaikovsky's ballet.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Maleficent curses the baby: Maleficent's name comes from Latin for doing harm; she is voiced by Eleanor Audley, who also voiced Cinderella's stepmother.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Merryweather softens the curse: Merryweather is the blue fairy, and the fairies' running quarrel over whether Aurora's dress is pink or blue is a film gag.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Fairies hide her in the woods: The fairies hide her for sixteen years, and their disastrous attempt to bake a cake without magic is a highlight.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Briar Rose meets Phillip: Briar Rose is the princess's name in the Grimms' version; Disney reused it as Aurora's hiding alias.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Aurora pricks her finger: In Perrault's 1697 tale the curse comes from an old fairy who was forgotten when the guests were invited to the christening.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.The whole kingdom falls asleep: The sleeping castle covered in briars comes from the thorn hedge in the Grimm tale, which part for the true prince.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Phillip escapes Maleficent: Phillip's capture in Maleficent's castle and his escape give the prince a real fight, unlike many earlier fairy-tale rescues.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.Phillip slays the dragon: The dragon transformation is a Disney addition, and the Sword of Truth and Shield of Virtue are the gifts that save him.
Disney's Sleeping Beauty, in story order.A kiss breaks the spell: The kiss is not in Perrault; in Basile's 1634 Sun, Moon, and Talia the princess wakes after giving birth to twins.

Beauty and the Beast, in story order.A prince is cursed: The 1991 Beauty and the Beast was the first animated feature nominated for the Best Picture Oscar.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.Maurice gets lost in the woods: Maurice is an eccentric inventor whose wolf-chased flight leads him to the Beast's castle.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.Belle takes Maurice's place: The story is based on an 18th-century French fairy tale by Gabrielle-Suzanne de Villeneuve, popularised by Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont in 1756.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.\"Be Our Guest\": Lyricist Howard Ashman wrote Be Our Guest; he died in 1991, months before the film premiered.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.Belle enters the West Wing: The forbidden West Wing is where the enchanted rose sits, with falling petals marking the curse's clock.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.Beast saves Belle from wolves: Beast's design mixed features of a lion, bear, gorilla and wolf, said artist Glen Keane.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.The ballroom dance: The ballroom was one of the first major uses of computer-generated backgrounds in a traditionally animated feature.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.Beast lets Belle go: Beast lets Belle go to help her father, the moment the film marks as real love: letting go.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.Gaston leads a mob: The mob song gives Gaston his big moment, while his rooftop fight with Beast ends the film's action.
Beauty and the Beast, in story order.The curse is broken: The 2017 live-action remake starred Emma Watson as Belle and Dan Stevens as the Beast.

Famous queens, by when their reign began.Hatshepsut: Hatshepsut ruled Egypt as a pharaoh and was shown with a false beard; her successor later tried to erase her images from monuments.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Cleopatra: Cleopatra VII was Macedonian Greek by ancestry, and she was the first in her dynasty to learn the Egyptian language.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Wu Zetian: Wu Zetian is the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right, founding her own dynasty, the Zhou, in 690.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Isabella I of Castile: Isabella backed Columbus's 1492 voyage, and she and her husband Ferdinand also completed the Reconquista by taking Granada.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Mary I of England: Mary I was nicknamed Bloody Mary because about 280 Protestants were burned for heresy during her five-year reign.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Elizabeth I: Elizabeth I's reign of 45 years saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588 and a flourishing of English theatre.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Maria Theresa: Maria Theresa had sixteen children, including Marie Antoinette, and she ruled the Habsburg lands for forty years.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Catherine the Great: Catherine the Great was born a minor German princess and took the Russian throne from her husband, Peter III, in a coup.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Queen Victoria: Victoria reigned for 63 years and gave her name to an era; until Elizabeth II, hers was the longest British reign.
Famous queens, by when their reign began.Elizabeth II: Elizabeth II reigned for 70 years until 2022, and she became Britain's longest-reigning monarch.
